targetSkill: Teach the student to synthesize multiple cognitive moves (inferencing, tone/mood identification, evidence citation, theme construction, character motivation) across a single passage to arrive at an integrated understanding of what the author is doing. The student is not performing one skill; the student is coordinating several skills simultaneously to construct a whole-passage reading.
mustHave: A passage that requires at least two distinct cognitive moves to fully understand — for example, inferring character motivation AND identifying tone, or tracking theme development AND citing evidence, or connecting mood shifts AND structural choices
Observable signals for each of the required cognitive moves — each skill the integration demands is itself evidence-discriminable within the passage
A whole-passage reading that is more than the sum of its parts — the integrated understanding reveals something no single skill produces alone
At least 2 paragraphs of prose, providing enough material for integrated analysis across multiple cognitive dimensions
An integrated reading that is discoverable from the passage alone — does not require whole-book context to construct
mustNotHave: Passages that only exercise one cognitive skill — integration requires multiple skills working together
Passages where the 'integration' collapses to a single dominant skill — if tone dominates and everything else is secondary, this belongs in tone_misreading, not here
Passages where the integrated meaning requires whole-book context — must stand alone
Passages where competing integrated readings are equally valid — no clear dominant whole-passage meaning
Paragraphs dominated by dialogue (60%+ quotation marks) where integration is what characters discuss rather than what the author constructs
Nonfiction biographical or memoir prose about real people's lives; integration analysis requires authorial fiction where multiple craft choices work together deliberately
Archaic or heavily poetic prose that obscures the integrated signals behind unfamiliar syntax
Integrated readings that require specific historical, political, religious, or cultural knowledge a 9th grader is unlikely to have
Extremely short passages (under 2 paragraphs) that lack room for multiple cognitive dimensions to emerge

tierSignals.tier1: Integration requires two obvious cognitive moves working together (e.g., tone + character motivation, or mood + theme). Each move is clearly signaled. Student can do each move and then combine them on first pass.
tierSignals.tier2: Integration requires three cognitive moves, or two subtle moves that need careful reading. Signals for each skill are present but not surface-level. Student must slow down, identify each thread, then weave them.
tierSignals.tier3: Integration is the only way the passage makes sense. No single cognitive move explains the whole. Student must track multiple craft dimensions simultaneously — tone shifting as theme develops as evidence accumulates as mood builds. Requires re-reading and synthesis.
